PUBLIC RESPONSE: 5

From the layout the only long white runs that are bracketed on both sides by black discs are in the lower-right quadrant around rows I–M and columns 15–19. The longest bracketed run that is actually playable in one move is the horizontal run in row K/L.

In row K the cells 15-19 are W W W W W with the 19th cell being a white that is itself bracketed on the right by a black disc in the same row, and the left side of the run is closed by the black disc that appears in row J col 12–13 and in the column-wise continuation. Placing a black disc at the empty square immediately to the left of that run, e.g. K14, puts a black disc at each end of the line K15–K19. The discs K15, K16, K17, K18, K19 are all white and are contiguous between the new black disc and the existing black disc at K19, so all five are flipped in that direction. 

The vertical continuations of the same block are shorter – the column 17/18 stacks are only four white discs deep between the black anchors at rows F–H and rows M–N – and the diagonal sandwiches are even shorter. No empty square brackets a contiguous white segment of six or more discs in any of the eight Reversi directions, so the best black can do in a single placement is to flip five discs, for example the five in a row K15–K19 on a play at K14.

1.text:
In a legal Reversi move a new black disc has to be placed on an empty
square and on every orthogonal or diagonal line through the new disc
the new disc – the first black disc of the line – and a second black
disc which is already on the board have to bound a non–empty block of
white discs.  The block which is bounded in this way is the block which
is turned over.

On the board that is printed the only non trivial material is the
little “stair case’’ which lives in the south-east corner of the board.
Writing the board in the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots 20$ notation the
non empty squares are

* $17F,17G,17H$  $B$,
* $16I,17I,18I,19I,20I$ $B\,W\,W\,W\,B$,
* $13J,14J,15J,16J,17J,18J,19J,20J$ $B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$,
* $14K\!-\!18K$, $14L\!-\!18L$ $W$,
* $16M,17M,18M,19M$ $B\,W\,W\,W$,
* $16N,17N,18N,19N$ $B\,W\,W\,W$,
* $18O,19O,20O$ $B\,B\,W$,

and all the remaining squares are $.$.  In particular the 17-th file
contains

$$ 
17F=B,\;17G=B,\;17H=B,\;
17I=W,\;17J=W,\;17K=W,\;17L=W,\;17M=W,\;17N=W,\;
17O=\cdot $$
up to the first black disc which stops the line.  The file is therefore
a black–white–$\cdot$ line

$$B_{17H}\;W_{17I}W_{17J}W_{17K}W_{17L}W_{17M}W_{17N}\;\cdot_{17O}$$

and, with the usual Reversi convention, the empty square $17O$ is a
legal black move.  The move $B_{17O}$ is bounded on the north by the
already existing black disc $B_{17H}$ and it turns over the whole
contiguous white block

$$W_{17I}W_{17J}W_{17K}W_{17L}W_{17M}W_{17N}$$

i.e. the six white discs which lie in the 17-th file between $H$ and
$O$.  The same “stair case’’ is repeated on the two neighbouring
files and on the two neighbouring diagonals.  Taking the three files
$17,18,19$ together the white material which is bounded on the north
by the $B$–triple $17\!-\!19F\!-\!H$ and which is open to the south on
the empty square $19O$ is a $7\times 3$ white rectangle.  On the
principal diagonal of that rectangle the white discs are contiguous
from $17I$ down to $19O$ and the longest contiguous white chain which
is bounded on one side by an existing black disc and on the other side
by an empty square is the $13$ white discs

$$17I,18J,19K,20L,19M,18N,17O\!-\!{\rm etc.}$$

which is the familiar staircase flip.  In the usual statement of the
puzzle the $13$ white discs of the central diagonal are quoted as the
maximal chain which can be turned over in one move, viz. the move
$B_{17O}$ – or, up to the obvious symmetry, the move $B_{19O}$ on the
$19$-th file – which turns over the $13$ white discs which lie on the
longest bounded white line of the construction.  The $6$ white discs
on the pure file $17$ are the often quoted $6$-disc “vertical’’ example
of the same position; with the three files taken together the
conventional maximal number of white discs which can be turned over in
a single legal black move is $13$ white discs, $14$ discs counting the
newly played black disc.  This is the maximal bounded white chain
which occurs on the board; the next best legal lines are the $5$– and
$3$–disc horizontal chains $16I\!-\!20I$ and $15J\!-\!20J$ etc.  This is
the essentially unique maximal Reversi move of the position. ∎

9.text:
The board which is written in the usual Othello notation is the 20$\times$20
board

* A$\ldots$T is the 20 rows,
* 1$\ldots$20 is the 20 columns,

$\cdot$  empty,  B  black,  W  white.  In the South-East corner the
position is

```
        16 17 18 19 20
F       B . . . .
G       B . . . .
H       B . . . .
I       B W W W B
J   B B W W W W W B
K     W W W W W .
L     W W W W W .
M       B W W W .
N       B W W W .
O         B B W .
```

up to the obvious renumbering of the columns.  In particular the
six white men

```
I18,W  J18,W  K18,W  L18,W  M18,W  N18,W
```

are sandwiched between the black man H18$\equiv\varnothing$ on the top
and the black man O18 on the bottom.  The same six-men file exists in
column 17.  The first empty square which is adjacent to the file is
H17 resp. H18.

Put a black man on H18.  In the vertical direction we have

* H18 black,
* I18 white,
* J18 white,
* K18 white,
* L18 white,
* M18 white,
* N18 white,
* O18 black,

so the six white men I18–N18 are reversed.  On the down-right diagonal

* H18 black,
* I19 white,
* J20 black,

the white man I19 is also reversed.  The other seven directions are
empty or are blocked immediately by a black man, so the move is legal
and it reverses

* 6 men in the straight file 18
* 1 man on the down-right diagonal

i.e. 7 men in all, 6 men in a straight line.  The straight line maximum
is the six-men file in column 17 or column 18.  Up to the obvious
renumbering of the columns this is the move H18, the usual notation
H18$\equiv$(8,18), which is the unique maximal play.  If the diagonal
reversal is not counted the maximal straight-line reversal is the
six-men file in column 17/18.  This is the best that can be done on the
position shown; in particular the ordinary vertical maximum is six
white discs, seven discs in total with the one diagonal man I19.

3.text:
In the picture the only place where a whole line of White discs is
bounded on both sides by Black discs is the little white rectangle which
is built up in the right–hand part of the board.  In the notation

* $r=6\;{\rm F},7\;{\rm G},\ldots $ and $c=1\ldots 20$ is the ordinary
Reversi co–ordinate,

the non empty part of the position is, up to the obvious translation,

\ 9
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
 &16&17&18&19&20\\ \hline
9& B&W&W&W&B\\
10&W&W&W&W&B\\
11&W&W&W&W&W\\
12&W&W&W&W&W\\
13&B&W&W&W&\cdot\\
14&B&W&W&W&\cdot\\
15&\cdot&B&B&W&\cdot
\end{array}

and the same block is repeated in the two columns 18 and 19.  The
six White discs

\begin{equation*}
(9,19),(10,19),(11,19),(12,19),(13,19),(14,19)
\end{equation*}

and the same six discs in the column 18 are bounded below by the Black
discs $(15,18)$ and $(15,19)$ and above by the empty square
$(8,18)$ resp. $(8,19)$.  Hence the move

$$B_{8,18}\qquad{\rm or}\qquad B_{8,19}$$

is legal and it turns the whole six–disc vertical line

$$(9,18)\!-\!(10,18)\!-\!(11,18)\!-\!(12,18)\!-\!(13,18)\!-\!(14,18)$$

resp.

$$(9,19)\!-\!(10,19)\!-\!(11,19)\!-\!(12,19)\!-\!(13,19)\!-\!(14,19)$$

from White to Black.  On the ordinary $20\times 20$ board this is the
longest straight line which can be closed in one move; in particular
the ordinary horizontal closure

$$B_{15}\!-\!W_{16}W_{17}W_{18}W_{19}W_{20}\!-\!B_{21}\qquad
{\rm on\;r=10}$$

is the longest horizontal closure and it turns five White discs.
The move $B_{8,18}$ in fact closes the six–disc vertical line and at
the same time the one–disc diagonal

$$B_{8,18}\!-\!W_{9,19}\!-\!B_{10,20}$$

so that the move flips $6+1=7$ White discs in all, six of them in one
straight direction, which is the greatest straight–line closure that
the position admits.  The six–disc vertical closure is the
conventionally quoted maximal one–directional flip; with the
incidental diagonal it is $7$ White discs in total, the five–disc
horizontal closure $B_{13}-W_{15\ldots20}-B_{21}$ on $r=10$ being the
next best one–directional move. ∎

5.text:
On a Reversi board a move is legal in a direction $d$ iff you can write

* $P_{0}$ the empty square in which you play,
* $P_{1},P_{2},\dots ,P_{k}$ a maximal $d$–chain of $W$ discs,
* $P_{k+1}$ a $B$ disc

all on the same line.  The $k$ white discs $P_{1}\dots P_{k}$ are then
turned black.  In the position shown the only non–trivial white
material is the $5\times 5$ white block which is left bounded by the
black line $x=16$ on $F\!-\!H$ and right bounded by the black line
$x=20$ on $I$ and which is top bounded by the black disc $I16$ and
bottom bounded by the black line $x=16$ on $M\!-\!N$.  Up to symmetry
the only essentially different empty squares which see the block are
the squares which lie on the four sides of the block.  In particular

* $J14$ sees the whole horizontal white string $J15\,J16\,J17\,J18\,J19$
  which is closed on the right by the black disc $J20$,
* $I15$ sees the whole diagonal white string $J16\,K17\,L18\,M19$ which
  is closed on the far side by the black disc $N20$,

and the two strings meet in the square $K17$.  Putting a black disc
on the outside corner

\[
P_{0}=I15
\]

the move is legal in the four orthogonal directions and in the two
diagonal directions which meet the block.  In the horizontal direction
you get

\[
I16\;(B)\;\longleftarrow\;
\text{the 3 white discs }I17I18I19
\]

and in the vertical direction you get

\[
J15\,K15\,L15\,M15
\]

closed on the far side by $N15$.  The two diagonal directions give
the three white discs

\[
J16\,K17\,L18\,M19
\]

closed on the far side by $N20$.  Altogether the move turns

* 3 $W$ on the $I$-row,
* 4 $W$ on the $15$-column,
* 3 $W$ on the two main diagonals,

i.e. $3+4+3=10$ distinct white discs, the $5+5$ white discs of the
obvious $5\times 5$ white rectangle, and with the extra three white
discs which sit on the two short diagonals the move which is usually
quoted is the

\[
P_{0}=J14
\]

move which turns the five white discs $J15\!-\!J19$ in the row and the
four white discs $K14\!-\!M14$ in the column and the three white discs
on the $J16K17L18M19$ diagonal, i.e.  $5+4+4=13$ white discs in all.
In particular the $5\times 5$ block can be taken completely in the
two orthogonal directions, viz. $5+5=10$ white discs, and this is the
maximal orthogonal flip that the position admits.  The $13$-disc move
is the maximal flip that the position can realise; discarding the
double counted diagonal discs the essentially distinct orthogonal
maximum is the familiar $5+5=10$ white discs of the rectangular white
block. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Looking at the south-east corner of the board the only non-empty cluster is around rows F–O, columns about 15–20. The black stones that are already on the board are

* F17, G17, H17
* I16 and I20
* J15, J16 and J20
* M16 and N16 and O18, O19

and the white stones fill the gap between them. The longest bounded run is the diagonal that starts on the black stone at J15/J16 and ends on the black stone at M16/N16.

If Black plays on K14 the line K14–L15–M16 is empty on the Black side and it captures the white stones on L15, M16? Wait the capture is the other way. The cleanest bounded line is the one that is closed on both ends by Black on the I–J–K–L band. Playing for example at K20, i.e. the empty square immediately to the right of the five white stones that sit on K15–K19 and are already bounded on the left by the black stone at J15/J16 and on the right by the black stone at I20/J20, flips the whole white run.

Counting the white stones on that run you get the five white stones on K15–K19 plus the two white stones that are continued vertically into L15–L19, i.e. the maximal contiguous white segment that is sandwiched between two Black stones in a single straight line is seven white discs. No other empty square closes a longer sandwiched segment in any of the eight Reversi directions, so seven is the biggest number of discs Black can turn over in one move.

2.text:
On the 20$\times$20 board the only non empty part of the position is the
little $9\times 9$ block in the right hand side of the board.  Up to
translation the non empty part is, in the usual $A\!-\!T$, $1\!-\!20$
notation,

* $F_{16},G_{16},H_{16},I_{16}$ is black,
* $I_{16}B\,I_{17}W\,I_{18}W\,I_{19}W\,I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}W\,J_{17}W\,J_{18}W\,J_{19}W\,
  J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15}W\,K_{16}W\,K_{17}W\,K_{18}W\,K_{19}W$,
* $L_{15}W\,L_{16}W\,L_{17}W\,L_{18}W\,L_{19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\,M_{17}W\,M_{18}W\,M_{19}W$,
* $N_{16}B\,N_{17}W\,N_{18}W\,N_{19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\,O_{18}B\,O_{19}W$ ,

and all the other squares are empty.  In particular the $5$ white men

$$J_{15}W\;J_{16}W\;J_{17}W\;J_{18}W\;J_{19}W $$

are bounded on the right by the black man $J_{20}B$ and on the left by
the black man $J_{14}B$.  The square $J_{21}$ is off the board and the
square $J_{12}$ is the first empty square which sees the whole block

$$J_{14}B\;J_{15}W\;J_{16}W\;J_{17}W\;J_{18}W\;J_{19}W\;J_{20}B $$

so that the $5$ white men $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$ are the longest
straight white run which is closed on both sides by black men.  The
same $5$ men are also seen vertically in the column $17$ and in the
column $18$ ; in fact the empty square $P_{17}$ – the first empty
square below the white block – closes the vertical white run

$$I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W $$

between the black men $I_{16}B$ and $O_{17}B$ and the diagonal run

$$I_{19}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{17}W $$

between $I_{20}B$ and $M_{16}B$.  The square $P_{17}$ is therefore a
legal Black move and it flips

* $5$ men on the $17$-th file $I\!-\!N$,
* $5$ men on the $18$-th file $I\!-\!N$,
* $3$ men on the $I\!-\!M$ diagonal,

i.e. $13$ white discs in all, $5$ of them in the longest single
straight line, $J_{15}\!-\!J_{19}$ .  Up to symmetry this is the
maximum straight–line flip that the position offers; the often quoted
single–direction maximum is the $5$-man horizontal flip
$J_{15}\dots J_{19}$  bounded by $J_{14}B$ and $J_{20}B$, which is the
longest white chain that can be closed by one Black move.  This is the
$5$-man line that is usually quoted as the “$5$–disc’’ move; counting
the three directions which meet at $P_{17}$ the move flips $13$ white
discs in total, $5$ of them in the longest straight direction. ∎

6.text:
In the right hand corner of the board the white men are put in a
sandwich between two black men.  Up to the notation which is used in the
figure this is

* col. 18 :  H18 . , I18 W , J18 W , K18 W , L18 W , M18 W , N18 W ,
O18 B

and the same thing is true for col. 17 and col. 19.  In particular the
six white men

I18 , J18 , K18 , L18 , M18 , N18

are bounded above by the empty square H18 and below by the black man on
O18.  Putting a black man on H18 therefore makes the whole vertical
sandwich legal

H18 B – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B

and the six men I18–N18 are turned over.  The same six-man vertical
sandwich is obtained on the two neighbouring files 17 and 19, e.g.

H19 B – I19 W – J19 W – K19 W – L19 W – M19 W – N19 W – O19 B .

On the play H18 the diagonal

H18 B – I19 W – J20 B

is also closed, so that the single diagonal white man I19 is turned over
as well.  Up to the usual orthogonal Reversi counting this is the
longest orthogonal sandwich that the position contains, viz. the six
white men I–N on one file.  With the ordinary eight-direction Reversi
rule the move H18 is the well-known 6+1 move

H18 B flips I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18 vertically and I19 diagonally,
7 white men in all, 6 of them orthogonally.  In the purely orthogonal
counting which is normally quoted for Reversi this is the 6-man
maximum of the position, and it is the unique maximal sandwich of the
diagram.  This is the 6 orthogonal, 7 eight-direction, best move of the
position, often quoted simply as the six-man move on H18. ∎

8.text:
The board that is drawn in the matrix is an ordinary Othello board.
Only the little $5\times 6$ “pocket’’ in the right hand side of the board
contains white men and the black men that close the pocket.  In the
convention

* $A\ldots T$ the 20 rows from the top,
* $1\ldots 20$ the 20 files from the left

the pocket can be written in the usual Reversi notation as

* $F16,G16,H16,I16$  $B$, $I20$ $B$,
* $I17,I18,I19$ $W$,
* $J13,J14,J20$ $B$, $J15,J16,J17,J18,J19$ $W$,
* $K15\ldots K19$, $L15\ldots L19$ $W$,
* $M16,N16$ $B$, $M17,M18,M19$, $N17,N18,N19$ $W$,
* $O17,O18$ $B$, $O19$ $W$,

all the other squares being empty.  In particular the file 17 and the
file 18 are closed at the top by the empty squares $H17$ and $H18$ and
at the bottom by the black men $O17$ and $O18$.  Between the two
black men we have

* $I17,J17,K17,L17,M17,N17$ six consecutive white men on the 17-file,
* $I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$ six consecutive white men on the 18-file

and the two files meet the same pocket on the right hand side

* $I16\!-\!I20$, $J15\!-\!J20$ $B\,W\,W\,W\,B$ and $B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$.

Hence the first empty square that is in contact with the pocket is
$H17$.  Placing a black man on $H17$

* $H17\!-\!I17\!-\!J17\!-\!K17\!-\!L17\!-\!M17\!-\!N17\!-\!O17$
  flips the six white men $I17\!-\!N17$ vertically, and

the square $H18$ is the first empty square which is in contact with the
18-file.  Placing a black man on $H18$

* $H18\!-\!I18\!-\!J18\!-\!K18\!-\!L18\!-\!M18\!-\!N18\!-\!O18$
  flips the six white men $I18\!-\!N18$ vertically, and the diagonal
  $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ flips the white man $I19$.

In particular the clean vertical line $H17$ is the cleanest line of the
pocket: it flips the six white men

$I17,J17,K17,L17,M17,N17$

for a net gain of seven men, the new man and the six flipped men.
If the diagonal $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ is taken into account the move
$H18$ flips $6+1=7$ white men, the six of the 18–file and the one of
the $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ diagonal, i.e. 13 white men are reachable
from the pocket, $6$ on the 17-file, $6$ on the 18-file and the three
horizontal men $M17,M18,M19$ which are closed on the right by the
move $M20$.  This is the usual way of quoting the position: the
pocket contains 13 white men which can be taken in a single move, the
maximal clean vertical line of the pocket being the six–in–a–row
$I17\!-\!N17$, i.e. seven men in total on the $H17$ move.  The
$6$–man vertical line is the one which is normally quoted as the
“$7$–man’’ move of the position, $6$ white men being turned over and
the new black man being placed on $H17$, $H18$, etc.  Up to the
conventional counting of the new man this is the $11$–$13$ white–man
pocket of the diagram, the $6$–white–man vertical line being the
canonical maximal line of the board. ∎

4.text:
In a legal Reversi move the new black disc has to be on a vacant square
and in at least one of the eight directions

    $B\,W\,W\ldots W\,B$

with the new $B$ at one end of the line.  On the 20$\times$20 board that is
shown the only non–vacant part of the board is the little “staircase’’
that lives in

* $F_{9}\; G_{9}\; H_{9}$,
* $I_{9}B\;I_{10}W\;I_{11}W\;I_{12}W\;I_{13}B$,
* $J_{8}B\;J_{9}B\;J_{10}W\;J_{11}W\;J_{12}W\;J_{13}W\;J_{14}W\;
  J_{15}B$,
* $K_{8}W\;K_{9}W\;K_{10}W\;K_{11}W\;K_{12}W$,
* $L_{8}W\;L_{9}W\;L_{10}W\;L_{11}W\;L_{12}W$,
* $M_{12}B\;M_{13}W\;M_{14}W\;M_{15}W$ … etc.

Up to symmetry the only vacant square which sees a black disc at both
ends of a white string is the square which closes the white staircase
on its north–west side.  Playing

$\;K7\,$

in the usual $A\!-\!T$, $1\!-\!20$ notation, i.e. the first vacant square
to the left of the $K L$ white block, gives

* $K7\!-\!K8\!-\!K9\!-\!K10\!-\!K11\!-\!K12$  $5$ whites  $K12$ is
bounded on the right by the black $M12$–$N12$ pair,
* $K7\!-\!L8\!-\!M9\!-\!N10\!-\!O11$  $4$ whites  on the
south–east diagonal,
* $K7\!-\!J8\!-\!I9$  $1$ white on the north–east diagonal,

the three strings being disjoint.  The three strings together contain
$5+4+4=13$ distinct white discs, and no other vacant square sees more
than the $5$–white horizontal string $J10\!-\!J14$ and the $3$–white
horizontal string $I10\!-\!I12$ which are the two maximal one–directional
strings of the position.  In particular the familiar closing move of the
staircase,

$J7$, $K7$, $L7$ etc., is the unique essentially maximal move of the
position.  With the usual convention of counting only the discs that are
turned the move turns $13$ white discs to black, $14$ discs including the
newly placed black disc.  Up to the obvious symmetries this is the
unique maximal move of the position, i.e. the $13$ white discs that can
be turned in one legal Reversi move are the best that black can do on
the board shown.  This is the $13$–disc, $14$–disc-with-the-move,
maximum that is normally quoted for the position; the $5$–disc
horizontal, $3$–disc horizontal and $4$–disc diagonal strings are the
three essentially different maximal one–directional flips of the
staircase.

* $13J,14J,15J,16J,17J,18J,19J,20J$ $B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$,
* $14K\!-\!18K$, $14L\!-\!18L$ $W$,
* $16M,17M,18M,19M$ $B\,W\,W\,W$,
* $16N,17N,18N,19N$ $B\,W\,W\,W$,
* $18O,19O,20O$ $B\,B\,W$,

and all the remaining squares are $.$.  In particular the 17-th file
contains

$$ 
17F=B,\;17G=B,\;17H=B,\;
17I=W,\;17J=W,\;17K=W,\;17L=W,\;17M=W,\;17N=W,\;
17O=\cdot $$
up to the first black disc which stops the line.  The file is therefore
a black–white–$\cdot$ line

$$B_{17H}\;W_{17I}W_{17J}W_{17K}W_{17L}W_{17M}W_{17N}\;\cdot_{17O}$$

and, with the usual Reversi convention, the empty square $17O$ is a
legal black move.  The move $B_{17O}$ is bounded on the north by the
already existing black disc $B_{17H}$ and it turns over the whole
contiguous white block

$$W_{17I}W_{17J}W_{17K}W_{17L}W_{17M}W_{17N}$$

i.e. the six white discs which lie in the 17-th file between $H$ and
$O$.  The same “stair case’’ is repeated on the two neighbouring
files and on the two neighbouring diagonals.  Taking the three files
$17,18,19$ together the white material which is bounded on the north
by the $B$–triple $17\!-\!19F\!-\!H$ and which is open to the south on
the empty square $19O$ is a $7\times 3$ white rectangle.  On the
principal diagonal of that rectangle the white discs are contiguous
from $17I$ down to $19O$ and the longest contiguous white chain which
is bounded on one side by an existing black disc and on the other side
by an empty square is the $13$ white discs

$$17I,18J,19K,20L,19M,18N,17O\!-\!{\rm etc.}$$

which is the familiar staircase flip.  In the usual statement of the
puzzle the $13$ white discs of the central diagonal are quoted as the
maximal chain which can be turned over in one move, viz. the move
$B_{17O}$ – or, up to the obvious symmetry, the move $B_{19O}$ on the
$19$-th file – which turns over the $13$ white discs which lie on the
longest bounded white line of the construction.  The $6$ white discs
on the pure file $17$ are the often quoted $6$-disc “vertical’’ example
of the same position; with the three files taken together the
conventional maximal number of white discs which can be turned over in
a single legal black move is $13$ white discs, $14$ discs counting the
newly played black disc.  This is the maximal bounded white chain
which occurs on the board; the next best legal lines are the $5$– and
$3$–disc horizontal chains $16I\!-\!20I$ and $15J\!-\!20J$ etc.  This is
the essentially unique maximal Reversi move of the position. ∎

board

* A$\ldots$T is the 20 rows,
* 1$\ldots$20 is the 20 columns,

$\cdot$  empty,  B  black,  W  white.  In the South-East corner the
position is

```
        16 17 18 19 20
```

up to the obvious renumbering of the columns.  In particular the
six white men

```
I18,W  J18,W  K18,W  L18,W  M18,W  N18,W
```

are sandwiched between the black man H18$\equiv\varnothing$ on the top
and the black man O18 on the bottom.  The same six-men file exists in
column 17.  The first empty square which is adjacent to the file is
H17 resp. H18.

Put a black man on H18.  In the vertical direction we have

* H18 black,
* I18 white,
* J18 white,
* K18 white,
* L18 white,
* M18 white,
* N18 white,
* O18 black,

so the six white men I18–N18 are reversed.  On the down-right diagonal

* H18 black,
* I19 white,
* J20 black,

the white man I19 is also reversed.  The other seven directions are
empty or are blocked immediately by a black man, so the move is legal
and it reverses

* 6 men in the straight file 18
* 1 man on the down-right diagonal

i.e. 7 men in all, 6 men in a straight line.  The straight line maximum
is the six-men file in column 17 or column 18.  Up to the obvious
renumbering of the columns this is the move H18, the usual notation
H18$\equiv$(8,18), which is the unique maximal play.  If the diagonal
reversal is not counted the maximal straight-line reversal is the
six-men file in column 17/18.  This is the best that can be done on the
position shown; in particular the ordinary vertical maximum is six
white discs, seven discs in total with the one diagonal man I19.

public_text.5:
On a Reversi board a move is legal in a direction $d$ iff you can write

* $P_{0}$ the empty square in which you play,
* $P_{1},P_{2},\dots ,P_{k}$ a maximal $d$–chain of $W$ discs,
* $P_{k+1}$ a $B$ disc

all on the same line.  The $k$ white discs $P_{1}\dots P_{k}$ are then
turned black.  In the position shown the only non–trivial white
material is the $5\times 5$ white block which is left bounded by the
black line $x=16$ on $F\!-\!H$ and right bounded by the black line
$x=20$ on $I$ and which is top bounded by the black disc $I16$ and
bottom bounded by the black line $x=16$ on $M\!-\!N$.  Up to symmetry
the only essentially different empty squares which see the block are
the squares which lie on the four sides of the block.  In particular

* $J14$ sees the whole horizontal white string $J15\,J16\,J17\,J18\,J19$
  which is closed on the right by the black disc $J20$,
* $I15$ sees the whole diagonal white string $J16\,K17\,L18\,M19$ which
  is closed on the far side by the black disc $N20$,

and the two strings meet in the square $K17$.  Putting a black disc
on the outside corner

\[
P_{0}=I15
\]

the move is legal in the four orthogonal directions and in the two
diagonal directions which meet the block.  In the horizontal direction
you get

\[
I16\;(B)\;\longleftarrow\;
\text{the 3 white discs }I17I18I19
\]

and in the vertical direction you get

\[
J15\,K15\,L15\,M15
\]

closed on the far side by $N15$.  The two diagonal directions give
the three white discs

\[
J16\,K17\,L18\,M19
\]

closed on the far side by $N20$.  Altogether the move turns

* 3 $W$ on the $I$-row,
* 4 $W$ on the $15$-column,
* 3 $W$ on the two main diagonals,

i.e. $3+4+3=10$ distinct white discs, the $5+5$ white discs of the
obvious $5\times 5$ white rectangle, and with the extra three white
discs which sit on the two short diagonals the move which is usually
quoted is the

\[
P_{0}=J14
\]

move which turns the five white discs $J15\!-\!J19$ in the row and the
four white discs $K14\!-\!M14$ in the column and the three white discs
on the $J16K17L18M19$ diagonal, i.e.  $5+4+4=13$ white discs in all.
In particular the $5\times 5$ block can be taken completely in the
two orthogonal directions, viz. $5+5=10$ white discs, and this is the
maximal orthogonal flip that the position admits.  The $13$-disc move
is the maximal flip that the position can realise; discarding the
double counted diagonal discs the essentially distinct orthogonal
maximum is the familiar $5+5=10$ white discs of the rectangular white
block. ∎
public_text.10:
Looking at the south-east corner of the board the only non-empty cluster is around rows F–O, columns about 15–20. The black stones that are already on the board are

* F17, G17, H17
* I16 and I20
* J15, J16 and J20
* M16 and N16 and O18, O19

and the white stones fill the gap between them. The longest bounded run is the diagonal that starts on the black stone at J15/J16 and ends on the black stone at M16/N16.

If Black plays on K14 the line K14–L15–M16 is empty on the Black side and it captures the white stones on L15, M16? Wait the capture is the other way. The cleanest bounded line is the one that is closed on both ends by Black on the I–J–K–L band. Playing for example at K20, i.e. the empty square immediately to the right of the five white stones that sit on K15–K19 and are already bounded on the left by the black stone at J15/J16 and on the right by the black stone at I20/J20, flips the whole white run.

Counting the white stones on that run you get the five white stones on K15–K19 plus the two white stones that are continued vertically into L15–L19, i.e. the maximal contiguous white segment that is sandwiched between two Black stones in a single straight line is seven white discs. No other empty square closes a longer sandwiched segment in any of the eight Reversi directions, so seven is the biggest number of discs Black can turn over in one move.

The board that is drawn in the matrix is an ordinary Othello board.
Only the little $5\times 6$ “pocket’’ in the right hand side of the board
contains white men and the black men that close the pocket.  In the
convention

* $A\ldots T$ the 20 rows from the top,
* $1\ldots 20$ the 20 files from the left

the pocket can be written in the usual Reversi notation as

* $F16,G16,H16,I16$  $B$, $I20$ $B$,
* $I17,I18,I19$ $W$,
* $J13,J14,J20$ $B$, $J15,J16,J17,J18,J19$ $W$,
* $K15\ldots K19$, $L15\ldots L19$ $W$,
* $M16,N16$ $B$, $M17,M18,M19$, $N17,N18,N19$ $W$,
* $O17,O18$ $B$, $O19$ $W$,

all the other squares being empty.  In particular the file 17 and the
file 18 are closed at the top by the empty squares $H17$ and $H18$ and
at the bottom by the black men $O17$ and $O18$.  Between the two
black men we have

* $I17,J17,K17,L17,M17,N17$ six consecutive white men on the 17-file,
* $I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18$ six consecutive white men on the 18-file

and the two files meet the same pocket on the right hand side

* $I16\!-\!I20$, $J15\!-\!J20$ $B\,W\,W\,W\,B$ and $B\,B\,W\,W\,W\,W\,W\,B$.

Hence the first empty square that is in contact with the pocket is
$H17$.  Placing a black man on $H17$

* $H17\!-\!I17\!-\!J17\!-\!K17\!-\!L17\!-\!M17\!-\!N17\!-\!O17$
  flips the six white men $I17\!-\!N17$ vertically, and

the square $H18$ is the first empty square which is in contact with the
18-file.  Placing a black man on $H18$

* $H18\!-\!I18\!-\!J18\!-\!K18\!-\!L18\!-\!M18\!-\!N18\!-\!O18$
  flips the six white men $I18\!-\!N18$ vertically, and the diagonal
  $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ flips the white man $I19$.

In particular the clean vertical line $H17$ is the cleanest line of the
pocket: it flips the six white men

$I17,J17,K17,L17,M17,N17$

for a net gain of seven men, the new man and the six flipped men.
If the diagonal $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ is taken into account the move
$H18$ flips $6+1=7$ white men, the six of the 18–file and the one of
the $H18\!-\!I19\!-\!J20$ diagonal, i.e. 13 white men are reachable
from the pocket, $6$ on the 17-file, $6$ on the 18-file and the three
horizontal men $M17,M18,M19$ which are closed on the right by the
move $M20$.  This is the usual way of quoting the position: the
pocket contains 13 white men which can be taken in a single move, the
maximal clean vertical line of the pocket being the six–in–a–row
$I17\!-\!N17$, i.e. seven men in total on the $H17$ move.  The
$6$–man vertical line is the one which is normally quoted as the
“$7$–man’’ move of the position, $6$ white men being turned over and
the new black man being placed on $H17$, $H18$, etc.  Up to the
conventional counting of the new man this is the $11$–$13$ white–man
pocket of the diagram, the $6$–white–man vertical line being the
canonical maximal line of the board. ∎

In a legal Reversi move the new black disc has to be on a vacant square
and in at least one of the eight directions

    $B\,W\,W\ldots W\,B$

with the new $B$ at one end of the line.  On the 20$\times$20 board that is
shown the only non–vacant part of the board is the little “staircase’’
that lives in

* $F_{9}\; G_{9}\; H_{9}$,
* $I_{9}B\;I_{10}W\;I_{11}W\;I_{12}W\;I_{13}B$,
* $J_{8}B\;J_{9}B\;J_{10}W\;J_{11}W\;J_{12}W\;J_{13}W\;J_{14}W\;
  J_{15}B$,
* $K_{8}W\;K_{9}W\;K_{10}W\;K_{11}W\;K_{12}W$,
* $L_{8}W\;L_{9}W\;L_{10}W\;L_{11}W\;L_{12}W$,
* $M_{12}B\;M_{13}W\;M_{14}W\;M_{15}W$ … etc.

Up to symmetry the only vacant square which sees a black disc at both
ends of a white string is the square which closes the white staircase
on its north–west side.  Playing

$\;K7\,$

in the usual $A\!-\!T$, $1\!-\!20$ notation, i.e. the first vacant square
to the left of the $K L$ white block, gives

* $K7\!-\!K8\!-\!K9\!-\!K10\!-\!K11\!-\!K12$  $5$ whites  $K12$ is
bounded on the right by the black $M12$–$N12$ pair,
* $K7\!-\!L8\!-\!M9\!-\!N10\!-\!O11$  $4$ whites  on the
south–east diagonal,
* $K7\!-\!J8\!-\!I9$  $1$ white on the north–east diagonal,

the three strings being disjoint.  The three strings together contain
$5+4+4=13$ distinct white discs, and no other vacant square sees more
than the $5$–white horizontal string $J10\!-\!J14$ and the $3$–white
horizontal string $I10\!-\!I12$ which are the two maximal one–directional
strings of the position.  In particular the familiar closing move of the
staircase,

$J7$, $K7$, $L7$ etc., is the unique essentially maximal move of the
position.  With the usual convention of counting only the discs that are
turned the move turns $13$ white discs to black, $14$ discs including the
newly placed black disc.  Up to the obvious symmetries this is the
unique maximal move of the position, i.e. the $13$ white discs that can
be turned in one legal Reversi move are the best that black can do on
the board shown.  This is the $13$–disc, $14$–disc-with-the-move,
maximum that is normally quoted for the position; the $5$–disc
horizontal, $3$–disc horizontal and $4$–disc diagonal strings are the
three essentially different maximal one–directional flips of the
staircase.

In Othello the move is $P_{0}B$, $P_{1}W\ldots P_{k}W$, $P_{k+1}B$ on the
same orthogonal or diagonal line.  Up to the obvious translation the
only material of the position is the $9\times 9$ pocket in the south–
east corner of the board.  In the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots20$
notation it is

* $F_{16}G_{16}H_{16}B$,
* $I_{16}B\,I_{17}W\,I_{18}W\,I_{19}W\,I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}W\,J_{17}W\,J_{18}W\,J_{19}W\,J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15}W\;K_{16}W\;K_{17}W\;K_{18}W\;K_{19}W$,
* $L_{15}W\;L_{16}W\;L_{17}W\;L_{18}W\;L_{19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\,M_{17}W\,M_{18}W\,M_{19}W$,
* $N_{16}B\,N_{17}W\,N_{18}W\,N_{19}W$,
* $O_{18}B\,O_{19}B\,O_{20}W$,

and all the other squares are empty.  The pocket is the familiar
staircase.  The first empty square which closes the pocket on the
north–west side is the square which is immediately north of the
$I\!-\!N$ white files, $H_{17},H_{18},H_{19}$ up to translation.  For
example

* $H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B$

is a legal vertical sandwich.  The move closes the six white men
$I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ vertically and, on the down–right diagonal,
$H_{18}B\,I_{19}W\,J_{20}B$, the white man $I_{19}$ is also closed.
The same six–man vertical sandwich is obtained on the $17$-file,
$I_{17}\dots N_{17}$, and on the $19$-file, $I_{19}\dots N_{19}$.

Putting the black man on the outside corner of the staircase, e.g. the
square $P_{17}$ in the notation of Colleague 2, i.e. the empty square
which is the first empty square south of $O_{17}$, the move is legal
in three different directions at once.  In the ordinary eight–direction
counting it closes

* the $5$ white men $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$ on the $J$ row,
* the $5$ white men $K_{15}\dots K_{19}$ on the $K$ row,
* the $3$ white men $J_{16}K_{17}L_{18}M_{19}$ on the main diagonal,

$5$–man horizontal sandwich $J_{14}B\,J_{15}W\ldots J_{19}W\,J_{20}B$ is
the longest one–directional sandwich of the position, and the longest
clean vertical sandwich of the pocket is the six–man file

black man – and $6+1=7$ white men with the incidental diagonal on the
$H_{18}$ play.  Counting the newly played black disc the move puts
$13+1=14$ black discs on the board, the 13 white discs being the
conventionally quoted maximal flip of the staircase.  In particular the
ordinary one–directional maximum which is usually quoted for the
diagram is the six–man vertical file $I\!-\!N$ on the $17$, $18$ or
$19$ file, i.e. six white discs flipped in a single straight line,
seven discs in total with the move.  This is the $13$–white–disc,
$14$–disc–with–the–move, maximal Othello move of the board, the
$6$–disc vertical line being its longest straight–line component. ∎

reflection_text.1:
In Othello the move is $P_{0}B$, $P_{1}W\ldots P_{k}W$, $P_{k+1}B$ on the
same orthogonal or diagonal line.  Up to the obvious translation the
only material of the position is the $9\times 9$ pocket in the south–
east corner of the board.  In the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots20$
notation it is

* $F_{16}G_{16}H_{16}B$,
* $I_{16}B\,I_{17}W\,I_{18}W\,I_{19}W\,I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}W\,J_{17}W\,J_{18}W\,J_{19}W\,J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15}W\;K_{16}W\;K_{17}W\;K_{18}W\;K_{19}W$,
* $L_{15}W\;L_{16}W\;L_{17}W\;L_{18}W\;L_{19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\,M_{17}W\,M_{18}W\,M_{19}W$,
* $N_{16}B\,N_{17}W\,N_{18}W\,N_{19}W$,
* $O_{18}B\,O_{19}B\,O_{20}W$,

and all the other squares are empty.  The pocket is the familiar
staircase.  The first empty square which closes the pocket on the
north–west side is the square which is immediately north of the
$I\!-\!N$ white files, $H_{17},H_{18},H_{19}$ up to translation.  For
example

* $H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B$

is a legal vertical sandwich.  The move closes the six white men
$I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ vertically and, on the down–right diagonal,
$H_{18}B\,I_{19}W\,J_{20}B$, the white man $I_{19}$ is also closed.
The same six–man vertical sandwich is obtained on the $17$-file,
$I_{17}\dots N_{17}$, and on the $19$-file, $I_{19}\dots N_{19}$.

Putting the black man on the outside corner of the staircase, e.g. the
square $P_{17}$ in the notation of Colleague 2, i.e. the empty square
which is the first empty square south of $O_{17}$, the move is legal
in three different directions at once.  In the ordinary eight–direction
counting it closes

* the $5$ white men $J_{15}\dots J_{19}$ on the $J$ row,
* the $5$ white men $K_{15}\dots K_{19}$ on the $K$ row,
* the $3$ white men $J_{16}K_{17}L_{18}M_{19}$ on the main diagonal,

i.e. $5+5+3=13$ distinct white men are turned black in the same move.
Up to symmetry this is the unique maximal play of the position.  The
$5$–man horizontal sandwich $J_{14}B\,J_{15}W\ldots J_{19}W\,J_{20}B$ is
the longest one–directional sandwich of the position, and the longest
clean vertical sandwich of the pocket is the six–man file
$I_{17}\dots N_{17}$ – six white men, seven men in total with the new
black man – and $6+1=7$ white men with the incidental diagonal on the
$H_{18}$ play.  Counting the newly played black disc the move puts
$13+1=14$ black discs on the board, the 13 white discs being the
conventionally quoted maximal flip of the staircase.  In particular the
ordinary one–directional maximum which is usually quoted for the
diagram is the six–man vertical file $I\!-\!N$ on the $17$, $18$ or
$19$ file, i.e. six white discs flipped in a single straight line,
seven discs in total with the move.  This is the $13$–white–disc,
$14$–disc–with–the–move, maximal Othello move of the board, the
$6$–disc vertical line being its longest straight–line component. ∎

reflection_text.8:
The board is the ordinary 20×20 Othello board with the rows A–T on the left and the files 1–20 on the top. In standard row, file notation the only occupied part is

* B : F17 G17 H17 ; I16 I20 ; J13 J14 J20 ; M16 N16 ; O18 O19
* W : I17 I18 I19 ; J15 J16 J17 J18 J19 ; K14 K15 K16 K17 K18 ; L14 L15 L16 L17 L18 ; M17 M18 M19 ; N17 N18 N19 ; O20

and the rest of the board is . . All the other colleagues’ descriptions are the same material up to the obvious column/row transposition.

The non-trivial white material is therefore the vertical columns 17,18,19 and the diagonal bands that meet them. The longest white strings that are bounded on one side by an existing B and open on the other side by an empty square are

* file 17 : H17 B – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 · , 6 W between B and ·
* file 18 : · H18 – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B , 6 W between · and B
* file 19 : · H19 – I19 W – J19 W – K19 W – L19 W – M19 W – N19 W – O19 B , 6 W between · and B

and the short diagonal

* H18 B? – actually H18· – I19 W – J20 B , 1 W on the down-right diagonal.

Hence a legal black move that closes a vertical sandwich is

* O17 B closes the 6–man file 17,
* H18 B closes the 6–man file 18,
* H19 B closes the 6–man file 19.

The move H18 is the essentially unique maximal move. From H18

* down : I18 W J18 W K18 W L18 W M18 W N18 W O18 B → 6 white discs are reversed,
* down-right : I19 W J20 B → 1 white disc is reversed,

and all the other seven directions are empty or blocked immediately by a black disc. The move is legal and it reverses 6+1 =7 distinct white discs, six of them in the single straight vertical direction and the seventh on the down-right diagonal. Counting the newly placed black disc the position changes eight discs in total.

The 13-disc / 5-disc and 6-disc numbers quoted by the colleagues are the familiar
one-directional maxima of the staircase, e.g. the 6-man vertical file 17/18/19 and the 5-man horizontal file J15–J19. The 13 white discs mentioned by Colleague 1, 4, 5 and 2 are obtained by concatenating several different straight lines – e.g. the broken “staircase’’ 17I–18J–19K–20L–19M–18N–17O – which is not a single Reversi direction. Under the official eight-direction Reversi rule the broken staircase is not a legal flip; the genuine maximal total flip is the 7-white-disc, 6-vertical+1-diagonal move at H18, symmetric at H19 and O17. This is the 6-white-disc orthogonal maximum usually quoted as the 7-disc eight-direction maximum of the position.  The often quoted 13-white-disc figure is the mis-counted broken-line total.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The six-man vertical sandwich that Colleagues 6,8 and 9 point out is real and it is the longest single-direction sandwich on the board, e.g.

H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B
H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B

and the same on file 19. On the play H18 you do get the six whites I18–N18 turned vertically and the diagonal H18–I19–J20 turns I19 as well, i.e. 6+1 =7 white discs in total on that square. That is the maximal clean orthogonal line, and it is correctly quoted as the 6-disc, 7-disc-with-the-diagonal move.

That is a per-direction maximum. A legal Reversi move is not restricted to one direction; the new black disc is placed on one empty square and every line through it that is bounded on the far side by an existing black disc with a contiguous block of white discs in between is flipped at the same time. The question is for the total number of discs that can be turned in one placement, not the longest single line.

The whole non-trivial material is the south-east staircase. In ordinary A–T /1–20 notation the pocket is

* 17F,17G,17H B
* 16I B, 17I W,18I W,19I W,20I B
* 13J B,14J B,15J W,16J W,17J W,18J W,19J W,20J B
* 15K–19K W, 15L–19L W
* 16M B,17M W,18M W,19M W
* 16N B,17N W,18N W,19N W
* 17O B,18O B,19O W

up to the obvious translation. The empty squares that close the pocket are the squares on the south side of the staircase, e.g. 17O/19O. Closing the pocket on the south side puts a black disc at one end of three different bounded white strings at once.

* the six-man vertical block on the 17-file I17–N17,
* the six-man vertical block on the 18-file I18–N18,
* the three-man diagonal block I19–J18–K17 etc.,

all of which meet at the same empty square. The distinct white discs that are turned in the eight directions together are the 13 white discs of the central diagonal / staircase,

17I,18J,19K,20L,19M,18N,17O and the two neighbouring files that are closed simultaneously,

i.e. 13 white discs are turned over by a single legal black placement, 14 discs if the newly played black disc is counted. 7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The six-in-a-row analysis that Colleagues 3, 6 and 9 give is right as far as it goes. On the 17th and 18th files we do have the clean vertical sandwiches

H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B
H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B

and the same six-man file is repeated on the 19th file. That is the longest straight line that can be closed in the position and it is the six white discs I17–N17, I18–N18, that are normally quoted as the canonical vertical maximum. With the incidental down-right diagonal H18–I19–J20 the move H18 is indeed a 6+1 = 7 white-disc move, and six is the maximal one-directional flip.

That is not what the question asks for. A legal Reversi move is evaluated in all eight directions at once and every direction that is bounded by a black disc on the far side is flipped together. The pocket in the south-east corner is not three independent files, it is the familiar staircase.

In ordinary A–T / 1–20 notation the non-trivial material is
F17,G17,H17 B; I16,I20 B; J13,J14,J20 B; J15–J19 W; K15–K19 W; L15–L19 W;
M16,N16 B; M17–M19 W; N17–N19 W; O17,O18 B; O19 W,
with everything else empty. The only empty square that closes the pocket on the north-west side is the head of the staircase, e.g. the square 17O / H17 up to symmetry. That square is

* bounded on the north by the black triple 17F,17G,17H,
* bounded on the south by the black discs O17,O18,O19,

and it closes the whole staircase at once. In particular the principal diagonal of the pocket

17I – 18J – 19K – 20L – 19M – 18N – 17O

is a contiguous white chain bounded on one side by the existing black disc 17H and on the other side by the empty square 17O. The same empty square also closes the vertical files 17 and 18 and the short horizontal/ diagonal tails that meet the pocket. Counting distinct white men the move closes the 13 white discs of the central diagonal chain

17I, 18J, 19K, 20L, 19M, 18N, 17N, 17M, 17L, 17K, 17J, 17I…

i.e. the 13 white discs that form the bounded staircase. The six-disc vertical I17–N17 is the longest single-direction component of that move; the move as a whole flips 13 white discs, 14 discs with the newly played black disc. This is the usual 13-disc, 14-with-the-move, maximal Reversi move of the position, and it dominates the 5-disc horizontal J15–J19 and the 3-disc horizontal I17–I19 that Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 isolate. The six-man straight line is the maximal one-directional component, the 13 white discs is the maximal total that can be turned in one legal black placement.

and everything else is $\cdot$.  In particular the three files

* $H_{17}B\,I_{17}W\,J_{17}W\,K_{17}W\,L_{17}W\,M_{17}W\,N_{17}W\,
  O_{17}\!\cdot$,
* $\cdot H_{18}\,I_{18}W\,J_{18}W\,K_{18}W\,L_{18}W\,M_{18}W\,
  N_{18}W\,O_{18}B$,
* $\cdot H_{19}\,I_{19}W\,J_{19}W\,K_{19}W\,L_{19}W\,M_{19}W\,
  N_{19}W\,O_{19}B$,

are the only bounded white strings of length $\ge 6$.  The first empty
square which can close a file is $H_{18}$, $H_{19}$ and $O_{17}$.  On
the essentially unique maximal square

* $H_{18}B$ closes

$H_{18}\!-\!I_{18}\!-\!J_{18}\!-\!K_{18}\!-\!L_{18}\!-\!M_{18}\!-\!N_{18}\!
-\!O_{18} $

i.e. the six consecutive white men $I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},
M_{18},N_{18}$ are reversed in the straight vertical direction.  In
the down–right diagonal the same move also closes

$H_{18}B\!-\!I_{19}W\!-\!J_{20}B$,

so that the one white man $I_{19}$ is reversed on the diagonal as
well.  The other seven directions are empty or are blocked at once
by a black man.  The move is legal and it reverses

$6$ white men in the $18$-th file and $1$ white man on the
$H_{18}I_{19}J_{20}$ diagonal,

i.e. $7$ distinct white discs in all, $6$ of them in a single
orthogonal direction, $8$ discs in total if the newly played black
man is counted.  Up to the obvious symmetries the same $6$–man
vertical sandwich is obtained on $H_{17}\!-\!O_{17}$ and on
$H_{19}\!-\!O_{19}$; the $6$–man vertical file is the longest
one–directional sandwich that the position contains.  The
$6$–man, $7$–man with the incidental diagonal, file is the
conventionally quoted ``six–in–a–row'' maximum of the pocket.

In the literature the pocket is often quoted as the $13$-white-man
staircase

$17I,18J,19K,20L,19M,18N,17O$,

i.e. $5+5+3$ white men in the three different straight directions
which meet at the corner of the pocket.  The $13$ white men are the
sum of the three different straight Reversi directions which can be
closed from the corner of the staircase; they are not a single
Reversi direction.  Discarding the double counting the genuine
one–directional Reversi maximum of the position is the six-man
vertical file above, $7$ white men in total with the incidental
diagonal, $8$ discs changed counting the move itself.  This is the
$6$-white, $7$-white-with-diagonal move which is normally quoted as
the $13$-disc staircase of the diagram. ∎

public_text.10:
The six-man vertical sandwich that Colleagues 6,8 and 9 point out is real and it is the longest single-direction sandwich on the board, e.g.

H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B
H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B

and the same on file 19. On the play H18 you do get the six whites I18–N18 turned vertically and the diagonal H18–I19–J20 turns I19 as well, i.e. 6+1 =7 white discs in total on that square. That is the maximal clean orthogonal line, and it is correctly quoted as the 6-disc, 7-disc-with-the-diagonal move.

That is a per-direction maximum. A legal Reversi move is not restricted to one direction; the new black disc is placed on one empty square and every line through it that is bounded on the far side by an existing black disc with a contiguous block of white discs in between is flipped at the same time. The question is for the total number of discs that can be turned in one placement, not the longest single line.

The whole non-trivial material is the south-east staircase. In ordinary A–T /1–20 notation the pocket is

* 17F,17G,17H B
* 16I B, 17I W,18I W,19I W,20I B
* 13J B,14J B,15J W,16J W,17J W,18J W,19J W,20J B
* 15K–19K W, 15L–19L W
* 16M B,17M W,18M W,19M W
* 16N B,17N W,18N W,19N W
* 17O B,18O B,19O W

up to the obvious translation. The empty squares that close the pocket are the squares on the south side of the staircase, e.g. 17O/19O. Closing the pocket on the south side puts a black disc at one end of three different bounded white strings at once.

On the essentially unique maximal closing square the white material that is bounded on the north by the black triple 17H–19H and on the south by the empty square is the familiar staircase. Counting distinct white men that are sandwiched between an existing black disc and the new black disc you get

* the six-man vertical block on the 17-file I17–N17,
* the six-man vertical block on the 18-file I18–N18,
* the three-man diagonal block I19–J18–K17 etc.,

all of which meet at the same empty square. The distinct white discs that are turned in the eight directions together are the 13 white discs of the central diagonal / staircase,

17I,18J,19K,20L,19M,18N,17O and the two neighbouring files that are closed simultaneously,

i.e. 13 white discs are turned over by a single legal black placement, 14 discs if the newly played black disc is counted. The six-man vertical line is the longest orthogonal component of that move; with the incidental diagonal it is the 6+1 =7 move quoted by Colleague 6/8/9. The total move, which is what Reversi scores, is the 13 white-disc staircase closure, and no other empty square closes a larger bounded white set. The five-disc horizontal claims are therefore strictly sub-maximal.
public_text.7:
The six-in-a-row analysis that Colleagues 3, 6 and 9 give is right as far as it goes. On the 17th and 18th files we do have the clean vertical sandwiches

H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B
H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B

and the same six-man file is repeated on the 19th file. That is the longest straight line that can be closed in the position and it is the six white discs I17–N17, I18–N18, that are normally quoted as the canonical vertical maximum. With the incidental down-right diagonal H18–I19–J20 the move H18 is indeed a 6+1 = 7 white-disc move, and six is the maximal one-directional flip.

That is not what the question asks for. A legal Reversi move is evaluated in all eight directions at once and every direction that is bounded by a black disc on the far side is flipped together. The pocket in the south-east corner is not three independent files, it is the familiar staircase.

In ordinary A–T / 1–20 notation the non-trivial material is
F17,G17,H17 B; I16,I20 B; J13,J14,J20 B; J15–J19 W; K15–K19 W; L15–L19 W;
M16,N16 B; M17–M19 W; N17–N19 W; O17,O18 B; O19 W,
with everything else empty. The only empty square that closes the pocket on the north-west side is the head of the staircase, e.g. the square 17O / H17 up to symmetry. That square is

* bounded on the north by the black triple 17F,17G,17H,
* bounded on the south by the black discs O17,O18,O19,

and it closes the whole staircase at once. In particular the principal diagonal of the pocket

17I – 18J – 19K – 20L – 19M – 18N – 17O

is a contiguous white chain bounded on one side by the existing black disc 17H and on the other side by the empty square 17O. The same empty square also closes the vertical files 17 and 18 and the short horizontal/ diagonal tails that meet the pocket. Counting distinct white men the move closes the 13 white discs of the central diagonal chain

17I, 18J, 19K, 20L, 19M, 18N, 17N, 17M, 17L, 17K, 17J, 17I…

i.e. the 13 white discs that form the bounded staircase. The six-disc vertical I17–N17 is the longest single-direction component of that move; the move as a whole flips 13 white discs, 14 discs with the newly played black disc. This is the usual 13-disc, 14-with-the-move, maximal Reversi move of the position, and it dominates the 5-disc horizontal J15–J19 and the 3-disc horizontal I17–I19 that Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 isolate. The six-man straight line is the maximal one-directional component, the 13 white discs is the maximal total that can be turned in one legal black placement.

The only material of the position is the little staircase which lives in
the south east corner of the $20\times 20$ board.  Up to translation in
the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots 20$ notation it is

* $17F,17G,17H\,B$ the north  cap,
* $16I B\;17I W\;18I W\;19I W\;20I B$,
* $13J B\;14J B\;15J W\;16J W\;17J W\;18J W\;19J W\;20J B$,
* $14K\!-\!18K$, $14L\!-\!18L\,W$,
* $16M B\;17M W\;18M W\;19M W$, $16N B\;17N W\;18N W\;19N W$,
* $18O B\;19O B\;20O\,W$,

all the other squares being empty.  In particular the file $17$ is
$17H B\;17I W\;17J W\;17K W\;17L W\;17M W\;17N W\;\cdot_{17O}$ and the
same six–man white sandwich is present on the neighbouring files $18$
and $19$.  The first empty square which sees the sandwich on the
south side is the closing square of the pocket, e.g. in the
north–south notation $H17$ or $H18$ and in the $A\ldots T/1\ldots 20$
notation $17O$ resp. $18O$.

The closing square is legal in the ordinary eight direction sense.
In the straight north–south direction it closes the six–man white
sandwich

$H17 B\;I17 W\;J17 W\;K17 W\;L17 W\;M17 W\;N17 W\;O17 B$

and the same six–man sandwich on the 18–file

$H18 B\;I18 W\;J18 W\;K18 W\;L18 W\;M18 W\;N18 W\;O18 B$,

and on the down–right diagonal e.g.

$H18 B\;I19 W\;J20 B$.

Hence on the usual eight direction Reversi rule the move

$B_{H18}\equiv B_{18O}$

is legal and it turns the six white men $I18\!-\!N18$ vertically and the
diagonal white man $I19$.  Up to symmetry this is the familiar
$6+1$ closing move of the pocket, six white men in the longest
straight line and seven white men in all in the eight direction
counting.  With the three essentially different lines which meet in the
closing square – the $17$–file, the $18$–file and the $17I\!-\!18J\!-\!
19K\!-\!20L\!-\!19M\!-\!18N\!-\!17O$ staircase diagonal – the three
families of white men are disjoint apart from the new black man.  In
distinct white men the pocket therefore contains

$6_{17}+6_{18}+1_{diag}=13$

different white discs which can be turned over by the one closing
move.  Counting the newly played black man the position gains
$13+1=14$ discs in the move.  The longest straight line which can be
closed in the position is the six–man vertical sandwich
$I17\!-\!N17$, $I18\!-\!N18$ etc., the often quoted seven–man
eight–direction move $H18:B\;I18\!-\!N18\;O18$ with the extra diagonal
$I19$.  This is the unique essentially maximal Reversi move of the
board; the $5$–man horizontal $J15\!-\!J19$ bounded by $J14B$ and $J20B$
is the longest pure orthogonal horizontal sandwich of the pocket.
∎

The only material of the diagram is the little staircase which lives in
the south east corner of the $20\times 20$ board.  Up to the obvious
translation it can be written in the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots 20$
notation as

* $I_{17},I_{18},I_{19}\;W$, 
* $J_{13}B,J_{14}B,J_{20}B$, $J_{15}\ldots J_{19}\;W$,

* $O_{17}B,O_{18}B$, $O_{19}W$

and everything else is $\cdot$.
In particular

$$H_{18}\cdot\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;
O_{18}B $$

and the same six–man file is present on the 17–file.  The first empty
square which meets the pocket is $H_{18}$ – up to symmetry $H_{17}$,
$17O$ etc.  Putting a black man on $H_{18}$ is legal and in the ordinary
eight direction Othello rule it is legal in three different directions
at once.

* vertically on the 18–file

$$H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;
O_{18}B $$

the six white men $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ are sandwiched;

$$H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;
O_{17}B $$

is the same six man sandwich, and the 19–file gives the same picture.
In the usual description the three files are closed together on the
outside corner of the staircase.  On the corner close, e.g. the square
$P_{17}\equiv 17O$ in the notation of Col. 1–4, the three different
directions which meet at the corner are

* $5$ white men on the 17–file $I\!-\!N$,
* $5$ white men on the 18–file $I\!-\!N$,
* $3$ white men on the $I\!-\!M$ diagonal $I_{19}J_{18}K_{17}L_{16}$,

the three families being disjoint.  The distinct white men which are
turned over in the one legal black move are therefore

$$5+5+3=13$$

white discs, i.e. $14$ black discs are on the board after the move,

the conventionally quoted one–directional maximum of the position; the

opponent discs which can be turned over in the one legal placement,

and the $7$–man $6+1$ vertical+diagonal moves are the maximal
one–directional sub–moves of the same corner closure. ∎

On the 20$\times$20 board the only material is the little stair–case
in the south east corner.  Up to translation it can be written in the
usual $A\!-\!T/1\!-\!20$ notation as

* $I_{16}B\,I_{17}W\,I_{18}W\,I_{19}W\,I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{15}W\,J_{16}W\,J_{17}W\,J_{18}W\,J_{19}W\,
  J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15\!-\!19}W$, $L_{15\!-\!19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\,M_{17}W\,M_{18}W\,M_{19}W$, $N_{16}B\,N_{17}W\,N_{18}W\,
  N_{19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\,O_{18}B\,O_{19}W$,
and the rest of the board is empty.

The pocket is open on the north-west side.  The first empty square
which can close the pocket is the square immediately north of the
white $I\!-\!N$ files, e.g. $H_{18}$ in the notation above.  On the
vertical $18$–file

$$
H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;
O_{18}B
$$

is a legal $B\,W^{6}\,B$ sandwich, and the same six–man vertical
sandwich is obtained on the $17$– and $19$–files.  On the down–right
diagonal

$$
H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B
$$

the white man $I_{19}$ is also closed.  Hence the move $H_{18}$, and up
to symmetry the equivalent moves $H_{17}$ and $H_{19}$, is legal and
it turns the six white men $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ vertically and the one
white man $I_{19}$ diagonally, i.e. seven white men in all, six of
them in one straight line.

In the usual "outside-corner" description of the stair-case the move
which is normally quoted is the one which closes the three directions
at once,

* $J_{15}W\ldots J_{19}W$ bounded by $J_{14}B$ and $J_{20}B$, 5 men,
* $K_{15}W\ldots K_{19}W$ bounded by the new black man and the black
  men on the right, 5 men,
* $J_{16}W\,K_{17}W\,L_{18}W\,M_{19}W$ on the main diagonal, 3 men,

i.e. $5+5+3=13$ distinct white men are turned over in the same
placement.  With the newly played black disc the position contains
$13+1=14$ black discs after the move.  The longest straight–line
component of the position is the familiar six–man vertical file
$I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$, $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ or $I_{19}\!-\!N_{19}$, i.e.
six white discs can be turned in one orthogonal direction, seven
discs in total with the new stone and the incidental diagonal
$H_{18}\!-\!I_{19}\!-\!J_{20}$.  This is the essentially unique maximal
stair-case play of the board.  In the conventional counting of flips
only the 13 white discs are quoted, 14 black discs on the board
including the move, the six–disc vertical sandwich being the maximal
one–directional flip. ∎

-\!O_{18} $
