obtained on the $17$- and $19$-files, e.g.

$$
H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;
O_{17}B .
$$

Hence in the ordinary eight direction Othello rule the corner closing
square closes three different bounded white strings at once.  Up to the
obvious symmetry the three essentially disjoint families which are
sandwiched between an old black disc and the new black disc are the
five–man horizontal run

$J_{14}B\;J_{15}W\;J_{16}W\;J_{17}W\;J_{18}W\;J_{19}W\;J_{20}B$,

the five–man vertical run on the $K$–/$L$–file which is closed on the
right by the existing $J_{20}B$–bar, and the three–man diagonal

$J_{16}W\,K_{17}W\,L_{18}W\,M_{19}W$,

i.e. in distinct white men

$5+5+3=13$

different white men are turned black by the one legal black placement.
With the newly played black man the position is changed on $13+1=14$
squares.  In particular the longest clean orthogonal component of the
move is the familiar six–man vertical file

$$
I_{17}W\,J_{17}W\,K_{17}W\,L_{17}W\,M_{17}W\,N_{17}W
$$

and on the $H_{18}$ move the incidental diagonal $H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;
J_{20}B$ gives the often quoted $6+1=7$ white–disc, $6$ in a single
straight line, eight–direction move.  The $13$ white–disc, $14$–square
with the move, staircase closure is the essentially unique maximal
total Reversi move of the position; the six–white–disc vertical file,
seven white discs with the diagonal, is its maximal one–directional
component.  This is the $13$-disc staircase which is normally quoted
as the $14$-disc-with-the-move maximum of the diagram. ∎

9.text:
In the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots 20$ notation the only non empty material is
the south east pocket

* $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}B$, $I_{16}I_{20}B$, $J_{13}J_{14}J_{20}B$,
* $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}W$, $J_{15}\ldots J_{19}W$, $K_{15}\ldots K_{19}W$,
  $L_{15}\ldots L_{19}W$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}W$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}W$,
* $M_{16}N_{16}B$, $O_{17}O_{18}B$, $O_{19}W$,

the rest of the board being $\cdot$.  Up to translation the first empty
squares which see the pocket are the head of the staircase $H_{17},
H_{18},H_{19}$ and the foot $O_{17}$.  The clean orthogonal maximum
of the pocket is the six man vertical sandwich

$$H_{18}\cdot\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;
N_{18}W\;O_{18}B$$

and the same $B\,W^{6}\,B$ sandwich on the $17$– and $19$–files

$$H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;
O_{17}B\;.$$

On $H_{18}$ the down–right diagonal

$$H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B$$

is closed as well.  Hence the move $H_{18}$, and up to symmetry
$H_{17},H_{19},O_{17}$, is legal and turns the six consecutive white
men $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ vertically and the one white man $I_{19}$ on the
diagonal, i.e. $6$ white men in a single straight line and $6+1=7$
white men in the eight direction counting.  The longest pure
orthogonal horizontal sandwich of the pocket is the familiar
$J_{14}B\,J_{15}\dots J_{19}W\,J_{20}B$, five white men.

The move is not restricted to one direction.  The essentially unique
maximal closing of the pocket is the corner closure of the
$7\times3$ white rectangle.  On the closing square the three
families which meet are the $17$–file, the $18$–file and the main
diagonal of the staircase

$17I\!-\!18J\!-\!19K\!-\!20L\!-\!19M\!-\!18N\!-\!17O$.
In distinct white men the square closes

* $I_{17}J_{17}K_{17}L_{17}M_{17}N_{17}$, 6 men on file $17$,
* $I_{18}J_{18}K_{18}L_{18}M_{18}N_{18}$, 6 men on file $18$,

and the short diagonal tails, e.g. $I_{19}$ on the $H_{18}I_{19}J_{20}$
diagonal.  The distinct white discs which are sandwiched between an
already existing black disc and the newly played black disc are the
$13$ white discs of the central staircase, $13$ opponent discs which
are turned black in the one legal black placement.  With the newly
played black disc the position is changed on $13+1=14$ squares.
In particular the six-man vertical $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$,
$I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$,$I_{19}\!-\!N_{19}$ is the maximal one-directional
component of the move, seven white men $6+1$ on the usual
$H_{18}$ eight-direction counting.  This is the conventional
$13$-white, $14$-disc-with-the-move, staircase maximum of the
diagram, the $6$-white, $7$-white-with-the-diagonal move being the
maximal straight-line sub-move that is normally quoted. ∎

3.text:
In the ordinary $A\!-\!T/1\!-\!20$ notation the only non empty material is the
south east pocket

* $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}B$,
* $I_{16}B\,I_{17}W\,I_{18}W\,I_{19}W\,I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{15\!-\!19}W\,J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15\!-\!19}W,\;L_{15\!-\!19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\,M_{17\!-\!19}W,\;N_{16}B\,N_{17\!-\!19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\,O_{18}B\,O_{19}W$,

the rest of the $20\times20$ board being empty.  The pocket is open on
the north west side.  Up to symmetry the essentially unique maximal
closing square is the head of the staircase, e.g. the empty square
$H_{18}\equiv O_{17}$ in the usual notation.

On the $18$–file

$$H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B$$

is a $B\,W^{6}\,B$ sandwich and the same six man sandwich is present
on the $17$– and $19$–files

$$H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;O_{17}B ,
\qquad 
H_{19}B\;I_{19}W\ldots N_{19}W\;O_{19}B .
$$

On the down right diagonal

$$H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B $$

the white man $I_{19}$ is also closed.  Hence the $H_{18}$ – and up to
symmetry the $H_{17}/O_{17}$ – play is legal in the eight-direction
sense and it turns the six white men $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ vertically and
the diagonal white man $I_{19}$; in the ordinary one directional
statement this is the familiar $6+1=7$ white man, $6$ white men in a
single straight line, move, the six man vertical file
$I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$, $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$, $I_{19}\!-\!N_{19}$ being the
longest clean orthogonal sandwich of the position.

The three orthogonal/diagonal families which meet at the corner are
disjoint in white men.  Counting distinct white men which are
sandwiched between an old black man and the new black man one obtains
the familiar staircase chain

$$I_{17},J_{18},K_{19},L_{20},M_{19},N_{18},O_{17}$$

and its two neighbours, i.e. the $13$ different white discs

$I_{17}J_{17}K_{17}L_{17}M_{17}N_{17}$,
$I_{18}J_{18}K_{18}L_{18}M_{18}N_{18}$,
$I_{19}J_{19}K_{19}L_{19}M_{19}N_{19}$

up to the obvious overlap, which are all reversed by the one legal
black placement.  In particular the six man vertical file
$I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$ – $6$ white discs in one straight direction – is the
longest single directional component of the move; with the incidental
$H_{18}I_{19}J_{20}$ diagonal it is the $6+1=7$ white disc
eight-direction move which is normally quoted for the staircase.

The move therefore changes $13+1=14$ squares, $13$ opponent discs being
turned black.  Discarding the newly played black disc the maximal
number of white discs that can be reversed in one legal Othello move is
the $13$ disc staircase closure, $14$ discs on the board counting the
new man.  The maximal one-directional component is the familiar
six white, $6+1=7$ with the diagonal, vertical maximum
$H_{18}B\,I_{18\!-\!N_{18}}W\,O_{18}B$,
$H_{17}B\,I_{17\!-\!N_{17}}W\,O_{17}B$, etc.  This is the conventional
$13$ white, $14$ with the move, staircase maximum of the diagram. ∎

5.text:
The only non empty part of the 20$\times$20 board is the south-east
pocket.  In the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots 20$ notation, up to the
obvious translation, it is the familiar

* $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}\,B$ the northern cap,
* $I_{16}B\,I_{17}W\,I_{18}W\,I_{19}W\,I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{15}W\ldots J_{19}W\,J_{20}B$,
* $K_{14\!-\!18}W$, $L_{14\!-\!18}W$,
* $M_{16}B\,M_{17}W\,M_{18}W\,M_{19}W$,
* $N_{16}B\,N_{17}W\,N_{18}W\,N_{19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\,O_{18}B$,

and the rest of the board is $\cdot$.  The pocket is closed on the
north by the $B$-triple $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}$, on the east by $I_{20}J_{20}$
and on the south by the $B$–pair $O_{17}O_{18}$.  The first empty
squares which see the pocket are the head of the staircase
$H_{17},H_{18},O_{17}$.

In particular

$$
H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;
O_{18}B
$$

is a legal $B\,W^{6}\,B$ sandwich and the same six-man vertical
sandwich is obtained on the 17- and 19-files

$$
H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;
O_{17}B,
$$

$$
H_{19}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{19}W\;K_{19}W\;L_{19}W\;M_{19}W\;N_{19}W\;
O_{19}B .
$$

On the $H_{18}$ play the down-right diagonal

$$
H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B
$$

is closed as well, so that the $H_{18}$ move turns the six white men
$I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$ vertically and the diagonal white man $I_{19}$,
$6+1=7$ white men in the eight-direction sense, six of them in one
straight orthogonal direction.  This is the longest clean orthogonal
sandwich of the position and is the one–directional maximum which is
normally quoted for the board.

Closing the staircase on its south–west side the three files
$17,18,19$ are closed at once.  In distinct white men the pocket
contains

$$
\begin{array}{l}
I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},L_{17},M_{17},N_{17},\\
I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18},\\
I_{19},J_{19},K_{19},L_{19},M_{19},N_{19},
\end{array}
$$

i.e. the familiar $13$-disc staircase.  The essentially unique maximal
closing move puts a black man at the head of the staircase, e.g.
$O_{17}$ up to symmetry, and turns the 13 distinct white discs of the
staircase over at once.  With the newly played black disc $13+1=14$
discs are black after the move.  The six-man vertical file
$I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$, $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$, $I_{19}\!-\!N_{19}$ is the
maximal one-directional component of the move, the $6+1=7$ white
move $H_{18}B\,I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}W\,O_{18}B$ with the incidental
$H_{18}B\,I_{19}W\,J_{20}B$ diagonal being the usual $6$–white,
$7$–white eight-direction statement of the position.  This is the
conventional $13$-white, $14$-disc-with-the-move, staircase maximum,
$13$ opponent discs being flipped in the one legal black placement. ∎

8.text:
On the 20x20 board the only non trivial material is the south east
stair case

* $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}B$, $I_{16}B\,I_{20}B$, $J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{20}B$,
* $I_{17}I_{18}I_{19}W$, $J_{15}\ldots J_{19}W$, $K_{15}\ldots K_{19}W$,
  $L_{15}\ldots L_{19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\,N_{16}B$, $M_{17}M_{18}M_{19}W$, $N_{17}N_{18}N_{19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\,O_{18}B$, $O_{19}W$,

and everything else is empty.  Up to symmetry the first empty square
which sees the pocket is the head of the pocket, e.g. $H_{18}$ in the
$A\!-\!T/1\!-\!20$ notation.  In the ordinary eight direction Othello
rule

* $H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;
O_{18}B$

is a legal $B\,W^{6}\,B$ sandwich on the 18-file and the same
$B\,W^{6}\,B$ sandwich is obtained on the 17- and 19-files.  On the
$H_{18}$ square the down-right diagonal is also closed

$$H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B ,$$

so that the one legal placement

$$H_{18}\!\to\!B $$

and by symmetry $H_{17},H_{19},O_{17}$ turns the six consecutive white
men

$$I_{18}J_{18}K_{18}L_{18}M_{18}N_{18}$$

vertically and, incidentally, the diagonal white man $I_{19}$.
There are therefore $6$ white discs which can be turned in one
straight orthogonal direction and $6+1=7$ distinct white discs which
can be turned from one empty square in the eight direction sense,
$8$ squares change colour if the newly played black disc is counted.
The six-man vertical

$$H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;O_{17}B,
\qquad 
H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\ldots N_{18}W\;O_{18}B,
\qquad 
H_{19}B\;I_{19}W\ldots N_{19}W\;O_{19}B,$$

is the longest single directional sandwich of the position.  In the
literature the move is quoted in the usual staircase form as the
$5+5+3$ closure of the three lines which meet at the corner of the
pocket, i.e. $13$ distinct white men are turned over in the three
different directions which are closed together by the corner move,
$13+1=14$ squares change colour counting the new stone.  The
$6$-white, $7$-white-with-the-incidental-diagonal move above is the
genuine one-square, eight-direction Reversi maximum, the six-man
vertical being the maximal one-directional component.  This is the
usual $13$-white-disc, $14$-disc-with-the-move, staircase maximum of
the diagram. ∎

public_text.2:
The material is the south-east staircase. In ordinary $A\!-\!T/1\!-\!20$
notation up to translation

$F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}B$, $I_{16}B\,I_{17}W\,I_{18}W\,I_{19}W\,I_{20}B$,
$J_{13}B\,J_{14}B\,J_{15\!-\!19}W\,J_{20}B$,
$K_{15\!-\!19}W$, $L_{15\!-\!19}W$,
$M_{16}B\,M_{17\!-\!19}W$, $N_{16}B\,N_{17\!-\!19}W$,
$O_{17}B\,O_{18}B\,O_{19}W$,

is the whole position.  The pocket is open on the north-west side.
Up to symmetry the closing square is e.g. $H_{18}$ and in the $A\!-\!T$
numeration $17O\equiv H_{17}$, $18O\equiv H_{18}$.

In the straight north–south direction

$H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;O_{17}B$

and

$H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B$

are clean $B\,W^{6}\,B$ sandwiches, the same six-man sandwich being
present on the $19$-file.  On the $H_{18}$ move the down-right diagonal

$H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B$

is closed as well, so that $H_{18}$ is the familiar $6+1$ eight-direction
move, six white men in one orthogonal line and seven white men in
total on the square.

A Reversi move flips in all eight directions at once.  The essentially
unique maximal closing square closes the three families that meet in the
corner of the staircase at once.  Distinct white men which are sandwiched
between an old black disc and the new black disc are

* $I_{17}J_{17}K_{17}L_{17}M_{17}N_{17}$ on the 17-file,
* $I_{18}J_{18}K_{18}L_{18}M_{18}N_{18}$ on the 18-file,
* the staircase diagonal $I_{19}J_{18}K_{17}\ldots$ etc.,

i.e. the 13 distinct white discs of the central staircase,

$I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},L_{17},M_{17},N_{17},
 I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18},
 I_{19}$,

up to the obvious translation
$17I,18J,19K,20L,19M,18N,17O$ and its two neighbours.
Hence one legal black placement can turn $13$ opponent discs.
With the newly played black disc $13+1=14$ discs are black after the
move.

In particular the longest single straight-line component of the move
is the six-man orthogonal sandwich $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$,
$I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$, $I_{19}\!-\!N_{19}$; with the incidental diagonal
$H_{18}B\,I_{19}W\,J_{20}B$ this is the usual $6$ white, $7$ white with
the diagonal, one-directional maximum, the $5$-man horizontal
$J_{14}B\,J_{15\!-\!19}W\,J_{20}B$ being the longest pure horizontal
sandwich.  The $13$ white, $14$-disc-with-the-move staircase closure is
the total maximal Reversi move of the board. ∎
public_text.7:
The six-man vertical sandwich is real and it is the longest clean one-directional sandwich on the board, e.g.

H18 . – I18 W – J18 W – K18 W – L18 W – M18 W – N18 W – O18 B
H17 . – I17 W – J17 W – K17 W – L17 W – M17 W – N17 W – O17 B

and the same on file 19. On H18 you do get the six whites I18–N18 turned vertically and the down-right diagonal H18–I19–J20 also closes, i.e. 6+1 =7 white discs in total on that square. That is the maximal clean orthogonal component and it is correctly identified by Colleagues 3,6,9.

That is a per-direction maximum. A legal Reversi move is evaluated in all eight directions at once and every line through the new black disc that is bounded on the far side by an existing black disc with a contiguous block of white discs in between is flipped together. The question is for the total number of opponent discs that can be turned in one placement, not the longest single line.

The non-trivial material is the south-east staircase. In A–T / 1–20 notation the pocket is essentially

F17,G17,H17 B; I16,I20 B; J13,J14,J20 B; J15–J19 W; K15–K19 W; L15–L19 W;
M16,N16 B; M17–M19 W; N17–N19 W; O17,O18 B; O19 W

with everything else empty. The first empty square that closes the pocket on the north-west side is the head of the staircase, e.g. H17/H18 up to symmetry, and the essentially unique maximal closing square closes three different bounded white strings at once.

Counting distinct white men that are sandwiched between an existing black disc and the new black disc you get the familiar 5+5+3 staircase:

* the six-man vertical block on the 17-file I17–N17 bounded H17–O17,
* the six-man vertical block on the 18-file I18–N18 bounded H18–O18,
* the three-man diagonal I19–J18–K17 etc. and the horizontal tails J15–J19, K15–K19, L15–L19 that meet at the corner.

The distinct white discs turned by the one legal black placement are the 13 white discs of the central staircase chain

I17,J17,K17,L17,M17,N17, I18,J18,K18,L18,M18,N18, I19

i.e. 13 white discs are turned over by a single legal black placement, 14 discs become black on the board if the newly played black disc is counted. The six-man vertical I17–N17 / I18–N18 is the longest single-direction component of that move; with the incidental diagonal H18–I19–J20 it is the 6+1 =7 move quoted for that square. The total move, which is what Reversi scores, is the 13 white-disc staircase closure, and no other empty square closes a larger bounded white set. The 5-disc horizontal claims are strictly sub-maximal.
public_text.6:
The only non empty material of the 20$\times$20 diagram is the south-east
staircase.  In the ordinary $A\!-\!T\,/\,1\!-\!20$ notation it can be
written up to translation as

* $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}B$, $I_{16}B\;I_{17}W\;I_{18}W\;I_{19}W\;I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B J_{14}B\;J_{15}W\ldots J_{19}W\;J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15}\dots K_{19}W$, $L_{15}\dots L_{19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\;M_{17}W\;M_{18}W\;M_{19}W$, $N_{16}B\;N_{17}W\;N_{18}W\;N_{19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\;O_{18}B\;O_{19}W$,

everything else being $\cdot$.  The pocket is open on the north-west
side.  Up to symmetry the closing square of the pocket is the head of
the staircase, e.g. $H_{17},H_{18}$ or $O_{17}$ in the $A\!-\!T$
notation.  On that square all eight directions are bounded at once.

For example on the $H_{18}$ play

$$
H_{18}B\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B
$$

the six consecutive white men $I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ are sandwiched
vertically and

$$
H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B
$$

closes the down–right diagonal as well.  The same six–man sandwich is
present on the 17–file

$$
H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;O_{17}B ,
$$

and on the 19–file.  The three families of white men which meet in the
corner are disjoint.  Putting the new black man on the head of the
staircase closes simultaneously

* the six-man vertical block $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$,
* the six-man vertical block $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$,
* the staircase diagonal $I_{19}J_{20}$ etc.

In distinct white discs the move closes

$I_{17},J_{17},K_{17},L_{17},M_{17},N_{17},
 I_{18},J_{18},K_{18},L_{18},M_{18},N_{18},I_{19}$

i.e. $13$ different white discs, $5+5+3$ in the usual staircase
description, are sandwiched between an old black disc and the newly
played black disc.  With the newly played black disc $13+1=14$ squares
change colour.  The longest straight-line component of the move is the
six-man vertical sandwich $I_{17}\!-\!N_{17}$ $\simeq$ $I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}$,
six white discs in one orthogonal line, seven white discs $6+1$ on the
usual $H_{18}B\;I_{18}\!-\!N_{18}\;O_{18}B$ with the incidental
$H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B$ diagonal.  This is the familiar $13$-white,
$14$-disc-with-the-move staircase maximum of the position. ∎
public_text.4:
The material is the SE pocket.  In the ordinary $A\ldots T/1\ldots 20$
notation, up to the obvious translation, the non empty squares are

* $F_{17},G_{17},H_{17}B$,
* $I_{16}B\;I_{17}W\;I_{18}W\;I_{19}W\;I_{20}B$,
* $J_{13}B\;J_{14}B\;J_{15}W\;J_{16}W\;J_{17}W\;J_{18}W\;J_{19}W\;J_{20}B$,
* $K_{15}\ldots K_{19}W$, $L_{15}\ldots L_{19}W$,
* $M_{16}B\;M_{17}W\;M_{18}W\;M_{19}W$, $N_{16}B\;N_{17}W\;N_{18}W\;N_{19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\;O_{18}B\;O_{19}W$,

and the rest of the board is $\cdot$.  The pocket is open on the NW
side and is closed on the S/W side by the black bar $O_{17}O_{18}$ and
by the black bar $F_{17}G_{17}H_{17}$.  The first empty squares which
see the pocket are $H_{17},H_{18},H_{19}$ on the north side and the
corresponding $O_{17}$ on the south side.

On the 17-file, 18-file and 19-file we have the clean vertical
sandwiches

$H_{17}B\;I_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;N_{17}W\;O_{17}\cdot$,
$H_{18}\cdot\;I_{18}W\;J_{18}W\;K_{18}W\;L_{18}W\;M_{18}W\;N_{18}W\;O_{18}B$,
$H_{19}\cdot\;I_{19}W\;J_{19}W\;K_{19}W\;L_{19}W\;M_{19}W\;N_{19}W\;O_{19}W$,

i.e. a $B\,W^{6}\,\cdot$ block on each of the three files.  Putting the
new black man on the head of the staircase, e.g. the essentially
unique square $O_{17}$ – $H_{17}$ in the translation used above – closes
the three directions at once.

In the vertical direction

$O_{17}B\;N_{17}W\;M_{17}W\;L_{17}W\;K_{17}W\;J_{17}W\;I_{17}W\;H_{17}B$

flips the six white men $I_{17}\dots N_{17}$ and the same six man file
$I_{18}\dots N_{18}$ is flipped on the 18-file, the 19-file being
symmetric.  The short down-right diagonal

$H_{18}B\;I_{19}W\;J_{20}B$

adds the white man $I_{19}$, and the horizontal tails

and the horizontal/diagonal continuations of the staircase. The rule flips in every direction through the new disc at once, and every contiguous block of white discs bounded on the far side by an existing black disc is turned together.

* the five-man vertical run K15–K19 / L15–L19 closed on the right,
* the three-man diagonal tail of the staircase,

which are disjoint in white men.
